provenance.instrument: Philadelphia Zoning Code, Title 14, 14-604(11) Accessory Dwelling Units, with 14-604(1) and 14-701
provenance.status_detail: 14-604(11) as amended by Bills 190612, 210075 and 210078-A. American Legal 2026 code. L&I checklist PZ_004 Rev 3.2022.
checks: Owner must live in the house or the ADU and record an affidavit and deed restriction before final occupancy (14-604(11)(e))
Only one street-facing entrance unless a second already existed (14-604(11)(h))
ADU must be inside the house or inside a detached accessory building that existed when the 2012 Zoning Code took effect (14-604(11)(c))
The district must not otherwise permit more than one dwelling unit (14-604(11)(d)(.2)(.b))
Historic properties also need Historical Commission review (14-604(1)(f))
provenance.notes: The code limits ADUs by overlay, not by council district. Seven overlays carry ADU text (see eligibility.overlay_bars). Most follow council district or ward lines, so the tool can place a lot by overlay list, or by council district and ward when the overlay map is missing.

path.note: Allowed when the lot meets 14-604(11). Zoning permit from L&I.

fallback_path.note: Checklist says an ADU is not permitted when the tests fail. Relief would be a Zoning Board variance. The variance section itself was not read.

building_types.note: Single-family use in a detached or semi-detached building. Attached only in historic structures.

overlay_bars.note: Each overlay section read on amlegal. /FNE and /NE cover Wards 56, 58, 63, 66 and bar all ADUs. /NDO, /FDO, /VDO, /EDO cover Council Districts 9, 4, 5, 8 and bar ADUs in RSA-5 and CMX-1 except historic structures. /SIX (Bill 260074, approved March 30, 2026) covers District 6 and bars all ADUs. /SEV (14-545) has no ADU text. The 2022 L&I checklist predates /SIX.

existing_structure_only.note: Inside the principal building or inside a detached accessory building, such as a garage, existing when the 2012 Zoning Code took effect.

historic_bypass.note: Designated or contributing historic buildings qualify in any district and in attached buildings, with no lot size test. The use must still be single-family.

types_allowed.note: Interior of the house or of an existing detached accessory building. No new structure.

max_share_of_house.note: No share-of-house limit in the section.

historic_exempt.note: Historic structures may exceed 800 sq ft.

max_height_ft.note: Every accessory structure for a residential use: max 130 sq ft and 15 ft unless the code says otherwise. Applies to a detached or garage ADU building. An internal ADU follows the district height.

accessory_structure_max_sqft.note: Applies to every residential accessory structure, so a new detached building could not hold an ADU by right.

internal_uses_district_height.note: The 15 ft cap is for accessory structures. A unit inside the principal building uses the district height.

setback_front_ft.note: Set per district. See districts table.

setback_side_ft.note: Set per district. See districts table.

setback_rear_ft.note: Set per district. See districts table.

setback_rear_alley_ft.note: No alley rule found for accessory structures. 14-701(6) lists yard projections but no accessory building exception.

separation_ft.note: No zoning separation rule found. Building code governs.

max_building_coverage.note: Max occupied area is set per district. See districts table.

family_only.note: No family relationship test in the section.

short_term_rental_banned.note: Limited lodging rules apply to the dwelling. Not mapped to ADUs.

spaces_required.note: Set per district. See districts table (Table 14-802-1).

value.text: City maps put a quarter or more of this lot in the Steep Slope Protection Area. Unless the lot has no slopes of 15% or more, or all digging and clearing stays at 1,400 sq ft or less, the City Planning Commission reviews the plan before a zoning permit. On slopes of 15% to 25% digging and clearing need an earth moving plan by a Pennsylvania licensed engineer, and on 25% or more none is allowed (14-704(2))
value.quote: On those portions of the lot where the slope of land is twenty-five percent (25%) or greater, no site clearing or earth moving activity is permitted.
value.applies_by: The mapped Steep Slope Protection Area on the Steep Slopes Map kept by the City Planning Commission (14-704(2)(a)), then the slopes on the lot.
value.exempt: Lots without slopes of 15 percent or more; development, earth moving or site clearing of 1,400 sq ft or less in all, outside the street; stream restoration projects (14-704(2)(b)).
value.adds: Prerequisite City Planning Commission approval before the zoning permit (14-704(2)(c)(.1), 14-301(3)(c)(.1)(.j)); a topographic survey by a licensed engineer or surveyor if the Commission asks (c)(.2); an earth moving plan by a PA licensed professional engineer, approved by the Commission, kept on site (e).
value.area_layer: City of Philadelphia Zoning_SteepSlopeProtectArea_r, record zoning.flags.steep_slope (a quarter or more of the lot inside)
value.note: A small detached unit may stay under the 1,400 sq ft disturbance exception. The digging for the foundation, path and utilities counts.

value.text: Our ground measure reads the spot for the ADU at 25% or more (a 1 m elevation model, not a survey). Inside the Steep Slope Protection Area no clearing or digging is allowed on such ground, and the Commission may ask for a topographic survey to settle where it is (14-704(2)(c)(.2), (d)(.2)). Ask the City Planning Commission

value.exempt: The 1,400 sq ft disturbance exception (14-704(2)(b)(.2)) is read to apply before (d). Ask.

value.text: Our ground measure reads this spot as sloped, 15% or more (a 1 m elevation model, not a survey). If part of the lot is in it, 14-704(2) applies. Check the Steep Slopes Map with the City Planning Commission (14-704(2)(a))

value.text: Our ground measure reads this spot as sloped, 15% or more (a 1 m elevation model, not a survey). Whether the lot is in the mapped Steep Slope Protection Area is not on file. If it is, the City Planning Commission reviews the plan before a zoning permit, and on 25% or more no clearing or digging is allowed (14-704(2)). Check the Steep Slopes Map
value.quote: These steep slope protection requirements shall apply to development, earth moving activity, and site clearing within the “Steep Slope Protection Area”

steep_slopes.note: Read on American Legal (2026 code, current) on 2026-11-14. Steep slope protection applies only inside the mapped Steep Slope Protection Area (14-704(2)(a)), with limits by the slope on the lot: 15 to 25 percent needs an engineer's earth moving plan, 25 percent or more allows no clearing or earth moving. Exempt: lots without 15 percent slopes and disturbance of 1,400 sq ft or less. The Commission reviews before the zoning permit. Said as a condition or a question, never as a bar.
